description: Key facts for this chapter, written by hand from the chapter text. Every entry links to the section that explains it.

people.name: Tiberius Gracchus
people.text: Tribune in 133 BC whose land law split Rome; murdered on the Capitoline.

people.name: Gaius Gracchus
people.text: His younger brother, tribune in 123–122 BC; died in 121 BC.

people.name: Cornelia
people.text: Their mother, daughter of a famous general, who raised and educated them.

people.name: Scipio Nasica
people.text: Chief priest who led the mob that killed Tiberius.

people.name: Opimius
people.text: Consul who crushed Gaius and built a temple of Concord.

dates.text: Tiberius, as quaestor, saves a Roman army at Numantia.
Tiberius’s land law; he is murdered on the Capitoline.
The land commission’s work slows after the allies protest.
Gaius goes to Sardinia as quaestor.
Gaius’s first year as tribune: grain law, colonies, juries.
Gaius proposes citizenship for the Latins; it fails.
The Senate’s first final decree; Gaius dies.
The land commission is closed, its work done.

terms.english: equestrians, rich men outside the Senate
